title: Iowa and Kansas will be first major college teams to play at Field of Dreams
content:
The Iowa and Kansas baseball teams will become the first power-conference college programs to compete at the Field of Dreams Ballpark, Iowa Athletics and Field of Dreams announced Monday morning.

The fall exhibition scheduled for Oct. 10 between the Jayhawks and Hawkeyes will take place during a different time in the season than the MLB games held there in the summer, when the lush, green cornstalks stretch at least 6 feet high. In mid-October, those cornstalks are withered, crusty and shorter. Harvest season will be underway in northeast Iowa, providing a golden brown ambiance surrounding the ballpark.

Kansas won the Big 12 regular-season and tournament championships and advanced to an NCAA super regional before the Jayhawks were ousted by eventual NCAA champion Oklahoma. The Hawkeyes finished 33-23 last season. Although the teams regularly meet in nonconference spring games, playing at the Field of Dreams would lack for agricultural appeal around planting season.

The Field of Dreams is located outside Dyersville, Iowa, about 20 miles from the Iowa-Wisconsin border. The exhibition follows a string of events in 2026 at the ballpark, which now has a permanent grandstand and press box. The stadium sits west of the movie site, which remains intact following the 1989 film “Field of Dreams.”

On Aug. 13, the Philadelphia Phillies and Minnesota Twins will meet in the third MLB game at Field of Dreams and first since 2022. The Northwoods League, which is a wooden-bat summer league consisting of college baseball players, held its all-star game and events at the site on July 7-8. The Northwoods League announced it will expand to Dyersville in 2027.

First pitch between the Hawkeyes and Jayhawks is scheduled for 1 p.m. CT.
